words.meaning: existing as an idea, estimate, or stated value rather than as something fully real or settled
words.example: The budget includes a notional amount for travel, but finance has not approved the spending yet.

words.meaning: involving the many possible ways that elements can be arranged or combined
words.example: Testing every device, browser, and account type created a combinatorial problem for the QA team.

words.meaning: based on choosing the most plausible explanation from incomplete evidence
words.example: Her diagnosis was abductive: the timing and error pattern made a failed update the likeliest cause.

words.meaning: examining how something develops or changes over time
words.example: A diachronic analysis showed how customer complaints shifted after each pricing change.

words.meaning: present as a secondary effect without being the underlying cause
words.example: The rise in support tickets was epiphenomenal; the real problem was a confusing product update.

phrases.example: We need to step on it if we want to reach the airport before rush hour.

phrases.meaning: find a precise solution that balances competing needs or avoids multiple risks
phrases.example: The proposal threads the needle between keeping prices low and improving service.

phrases.meaning: an informal way to say that two supposedly different things have essentially the same result
phrases.example: Whether we leave at six or six fifteen, it is the same difference once traffic backs up.

phrases.meaning: an informal way to say that the same reasonable standard should apply to everyone
phrases.example: I covered your shift last week, so fair is fair—you can cover mine on Friday.

phrases.meaning: stop acting as though you are morally or intellectually superior to others
phrases.example: He needs to get off his high horse and listen to why the team disagrees.
